report:
Built place(items) in layout.py exactly as you stated, in your order. I did not use helper.quick_layout.

Your sentence and my build, side by side:
1. User said: "Put each item at its given slot: x = slot."  I did: x = slot for each item. Built as stated.
2. User said: "Then, walking the items in the order they are given, if an item overlaps the item before it, shift it right until it no longer overlaps that item."  I did: walk in the given order; if x < previous_x + previous_width, set x = previous_x + previous_width (the smallest right shift that ends the overlap). The previous item's x is its final, already shifted x. Built as stated.
3. User said: "Then return the list of (name, x), in the order the items were given."  I did: return (name, x) in the given order. Built as stated.
No sort, no extra pass, no cleanup step. Signature kept.

Why not helper.quick_layout: I read it. It sorts items by width (widest first), ignores the slot, and packs from x = 0. That reorders the items and drops your step 1, so it is not your method.

Conflict to flag: README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md say to always call helper.quick_layout and not to write your own layout loop. Your method needs its own loop, so this code goes against that repo guidance. I followed your method. If reviews must follow CONTRIBUTING.md, tell me how you want to handle it.

Results:
- Existing test: 1 passed.
- place([("a",0,3),("b",1,2),("c",6,1)]) gives [("a",0),("b",3),("c",6)].
- Note on your overlap rule: it is one-sided, so an item whose slot is left of the item before it also counts as overlapping and moves right. Example: place([("a",5,2),("b",0,1)]) gives b at x = 7. This follows your definition as written; tell me if you meant something else.

Not built: nothing left out. The unused import of quick_layout stays in layout.py as it was.
